propositions: The copied _legacy_convert oracle shares mutable _PANDOC_TO constant with production _convert, preventing independent mutation detection; immutable expected outputs must replace subprocess invocation for the legacy half while preserving all 884 real production Pandoc calls.

Pandoc 3.6.1 binaries differ by platform (macOS arm64 SHA-256 94ebf1efbce3561379e8f25de3efe5aeabee64dc36dd8e8b9e96cf05b4195c52 vs Linux x86_64 SHA-256 4715627586c5d9c732e8f5a6b6bb9e27c4216a76a7729e043b24374dedf8a1f0); the fixture schema must store a platform-keyed fingerprint map and select by current platform to reject cross-platform mismatches.

Golden fixture metadata must record exact generating Pandoc version, complete supported-platform binary-fingerprint map, deterministic regeneration command, and fast installed-version/hash drift assertion.
Format mutation from default to plain must fail the independent byte-equivalence oracle (RED) to prove fixture immutability and independent oracle contract.

Elimination of 884 copied Pandoc subprocesses measured 32.3766s local savings (49.4 percent) while preserving corpus cardinality, timeout/group-reap hardening coverage, and per-change production conversion verification.
